rgb: This downward-facing head-mounted view shows a landscaped outdoor area, with large boulders set in mulch and dirt to the left and ahead and a grassy lawn along the right. During frames two to four, the wearer moves backward and rotates slightly to the right toward the lawn, holding the grey bin's rim with their left hand in frames two and three, then raising it and supporting it with both hands directly before their torso at roughly 0.3 to 0.5 metres in frame four. depth: The monocular depth image depicts an overhead outdoor view in which the camera wearer looks down over their own bright-white torso and arms, 0.1 to 0.6 m away, while standing above mid-grey boulders clustered on the left, 1.0 to 1.8 m below the head, and darker areas of grass and mulch on the right, 1.5 to 2.0 m down. A grey plastic bin is positioned at the lower left, within the wearer's reach and 0.5 to 1.2 m away. To the right, a second person stands about 1.2 to 1.8 m from the wearer and 1.0 to 1.5 m from the rocks; only their lower legs, right hand, and a long-handled tool enter from the frame's right edge, with their head and upper body remaining outside the view. This makes it impossible to tell whether they are looking at the wearer, although their feet point left toward the wearer and rocks. Over the five frames, the wearer backs up and turns slightly clockwise away from the boulders, whose distance changes from 0.6 m and within reach in frame 1 to 1.5 m in frame 5. They lift and angle the bin using both hands in frame 4, place it at the lower left in frame 5, and extend their right arm forward about 0.6 m to take hold of the tool handle, which is within the second person's reach at the upper right. Compared with the flat RGB view, the depth map more clearly exposes the boulders' three-dimensional relief and stepped heights, the inner depth of the tilted bin, and the overhanging bush foliage at the upper left in frames 4 and 5. Nevertheless, depth is unreliable within the bin's dark opening in frame 1, where it appears falsely deep, and along the narrow tool shaft in frames 3 and 4, where it merges with the dark ground plane.
segmentation: The segmentation view extracts foreground objects and body regions against an unlabelled black field, entirely excluding the boulders, mulch, and lawn located 1.0 to 2.0 m beneath the camera. In frame 1, the camera wearer's left arm, torso, and right arm—0.1 to 0.6 m away and projecting forward and downward from the bottom edge—are divided into three separate 'person' masks, while the nearby bin at the lower left is missed. In frames 2 and 3, as the wearer backs away from the boulders and pivots right, their torso, legs, and right arm combine into one central 'person' region spanning 0.1 to 1.2 m. The second person's legs, entering at the right edge in frames 3 and 4, are segmented at middle right; they are 1.2 to 1.8 m from the wearer and face left toward them, with the upper body occluded beyond the frame. In frame 5, the second person's tool-holding hand at the upper right—about 0.8 m from the wearer and reachable by both people—and their lower torso on the far right appear as separate masks from the wearer's extended right arm. Relative to RGB alone, the segmentation clearly defines the separation between the wearer's hands and the bin being held in frame 4, along with the precise outline of the wearer's loose-fitting shirt and arms against the textured surface. Its categories and coverage are highly unreliable, however: the grey bin held 0.5 to 0.9 m away in frame 4 is incorrectly labelled a 'cell phone', and the other person's legs in frames 3 and 4 are wrongly classified as a 'cow' and 'horse'. It also omits the bin completely in frames 1–3 and 5, as well as the tool shaft and boulders.
pose: The pose output displays only magenta 2D hand skeletons over a fully black background. No yellow body skeletons are identified in any of the five frames because the head-mounted camera points steeply down at the wearer's own torso, 0.1 to 1.5 m below, and crops the person on the right to just their legs and hand, 1.2 to 1.8 m away. Frame 1 contains one open-hand skeleton in the upper right, marking the wearer's right hand pressed flat onto a boulder within reach at approximately 0.6 m; the left arm at upper left is partly outside the image and receives no mapping. In frame 2, after the wearer lets go of the rock and steps back slightly, both hands are tracked: the left grips the bin's rim at the lower left around 0.5 m away, while the right floats above the rocks and pants around 0.6 m away, with roughly 0.5 m separating the hands. Frame 3 has no pose marks at all, even though RGB shows the wearer's right hand and the second person's feet. Frame 4 detects both wearer hands holding opposing sides of the tilted bin rim, approximately 0.4 to 0.6 m in front of the torso and about 0.3 m apart. Frame 5 is blank again despite both people's hands grasping the tool shaft in the upper right around 0.6 to 0.8 m away. When detections exist, the map exposes precise finger positioning, palm direction, and grip shape on the boulder and bin rim that are difficult to distinguish in RGB because of similar skin and surface colours. Still, it performs unreliably when hands are partly self-occluded, blurred by motion, or close to image borders in frames 1, 3, and 5, and conveys nothing about whole-body pose or gaze direction.
